scope: Same initial public seed, historicalc582 source, exact separately compiled direct JVP. Independent saved-array arithmetic review only; no rerun of the physical operator and no production AD or fused-runtime benchmark.
conclusions: Original JAXrestart40/maxcycles20 passes this initial linear problem in21 total products. It does not show pathological800-product iteration.
SciPyrestart40 and80 give identical solutions/histories and20 total products. The smaller restart is not the limiting factor in this control.
Replacing the JAX limits by80/4 fails its unchanged true residual criterion. Host SciPy settings do not transfer directly.
Scalar normalization alone returns an internally accepted but externally invalid solution. The mandatory true residual gate detects this.
One explicitly stricter warm retry restores acceptance, but combined21 products and347.37s do not improve on original21 products and327.53s under this diagnostic.
No solver change is recommended on these results. The actual public positive-primal result remains supported in its own near-root/compiler scope.
limitations: The diagnostic callback has additional execution overhead; its timings are not the fused public executable timing.
This is the first linear problem, not later Newton correction solves or line-search trial merit solves. Those stages could have different conditioning or cost.
The source stopping formulas mix preconditioned and unpreconditioned scales. This potential robustness issue does not prove it caused the observed long public run.
Installed JAXzero-Arnoldi fallback takes a preconditioned Richardson step, as verified separately; it should not be called an empty unchanged iteration.
Actual public stage-level counters/timing would be the next causal cost diagnostic before introducing a wrapper. Original scientific and true linear criteria must remain unchanged.
publication: Local unpublished numerical diagnostic. No raw stellar arrays are included in retained solution NPZ files; no remote URL is asserted.
